about: Mapped hotels (OpenStreetMap tourism=hotel inside the country outline) as a share of officially registered hotels.

ES.counts: Hoteles (10,006) plus hostales (6,944) open in the month, establishments registered with regional tourism authorities. Hostales are included because OpenStreetMap often tags them as hotels.
ES.publisher: INE, Encuesta de Ocupación Hotelera, table 2011

MA.counts: Classified hotels, 1 to 5 stars. Unclassified hotels are not counted; riads and maisons d'hôtes (2,534) are counted separately.
MA.publisher: HCP, Annuaire statistique du Maroc 2025, table 10-2, from Ministry of Tourism data
MA.doubts: Morocco reformed hotel classification in 2025, so later editions may count differently.

DZ.counts: Hotels and similar establishments (ISIC 5510), all types, classified and unclassified.
DZ.publisher: UN Tourism Statistics Database, December 2025 release, as reported by Algeria
DZ.doubts: Official figures conflict: 1,638 for 2023, and ministry statements of about 1,467 in 2026.

TN.counts: Hotels, classified 1 to 5 stars (557) plus unclassified hotels. All accommodation types: 895.
TN.doubts: Registered, not operating: many registered hotels are reported closed.

LY.doubts: No official count since 2008, before the conflict.

EG.counts: Hotels and similar establishments (ISIC 5510), not split into land hotels, tourist villages and Nile cruise boats.
EG.publisher: UN Tourism Statistics Database, as reported by Egypt
EG.doubts: Nothing newer found. The same 2022 submission nearly doubles Egypt's room count from 2021, so its quality is doubtful.

SA.counts: Licensed hotels. Serviced apartments and other licensed facilities (3,258) are excluded.
SA.doubts: Rising fast as licensing expands (2,527 a year earlier), so it measures licensing as well as hotels.

YE.doubts: No official count since the war began; the last is from 2010.
